plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked atmospheric-composition and heat-trapping chart shows visible sunlight warming the ground and outgoing thermal infrared escaping freely through 99% of dry air (78% N₂ + 21% O₂ = 0% IR absorption) while trace water vapour and carbon dioxide (~0.04% / 4 in 10,000 molecules) absorb and re-radiate infrared, raising Earth's average surface temperature by ~33 °C (from −18 °C to +15 °C).

teach_overlay.label: 99% N₂ + O₂ (TRANSPARENT TO IR) VS TRACE CO₂ & H₂O (−18 °C → +15 °C = +33 °C)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked atmospheric-composition & heat-trapping chart on period paper showing 99% of dry air (78% N₂ + 21% O₂) absorbing 0% of outgoing thermal infrared vs trace CO₂ (~0.03%–0.04%) and water vapour raising Earth's average temperature by ~33 °C (from −18 °C to +15 °C)
teach_overlay.scale: carbon dioxide makes up just four molecules out of every ten thousand in dry air — yet together with water vapour it keeps Earth thirty-three degrees Celsius warmer than a frozen bare rock
